decisions.reason: As a secure document-storage feature closely tied to the firm's identity platform, it is likely inexpensive to carry and still has option value while demand in regulated sectors remains uncertain.

As a standalone identity-bound wallet it appears to overlap with the firm's broader payment and platform offerings, so in a portfolio with several adjacent options management would be relatively willing to prune it if traction is not yet clear.

The NFC-tag login authenticator looks more niche and less central to the firm's software-platform direction, so without strong evidence of uptake the option is more likely to be closed than funded further.
A secure payment and wallet framework fits the firm's core payments-and-identity stack and had enough prominence to merit its own page, so uncertainty still argues for keeping it on the market.
Because this product is presented as the firm's flagship strategic direction, management is very unlikely to remove it within a year and would instead continue investing behind it.

The application-shielding library draws directly on the firm's long-standing security capabilities and can complement both the platform and other offerings, so its option value remains high relative to likely carrying costs.
